Before the switch, two of the seven analysed states used justices of the peace (West Virginia, Arizona), two used coroners (New Mexico, New Jersey), and one each used a physician coroner (Massachusetts), a locally appointed physician (New Hampshire) and a magistrate coroner (Alaska) (Table 1; Delaware and Florida were excluded from analysis). The paper specifies one difference-in-differences equation for the pooled state-year observations, fitted over three time windows, and states no adjustment for repeated observations within a state. Figure 1 shows differing descriptive trajectories and relative levels: after the switch New Jersey remains above New York; New Mexico and, in most later post-switch years, West Virginia are below Idaho and Indiana; Massachusetts is below Pennsylvania both before and after its switch; and Arizona and Nevada show broadly similar post-switch movements. The authors attribute the sharp common drops in the first four pairs to the introduction of ICD-9 coding, with a comparable drop occurring before the Massachusetts switch. No state-specific reform-effect estimates or formal test of effect heterogeneity is reported, so these plots alone do not show that reform had different causal effects in different states.

evidence_set: The Results report higher harm-reduction support after the older rather than the younger person's story (F(1,1230)=4.5, p=.035), but print the means in the order 22.98 (SD 5.09) versus 23.57 (SD 4.78). They report no significant main effect of gender (printed F=.0, p=.802) or drug (printed F=.0, p=.922). A profile-plot discussion of the age-by-drug interaction describes higher support after the older rather than younger person in the ecstasy story, while printing F(1,1230)=4.8, p=.029 and means 22.7 (SD 5.4) versus 23.89 (SD 4.67). Table 1 stigma condition means range from 38.6 for Jane/younger/ecstasy to 50.1 for John/older/heroin. Independent editorial calculations using the rounded Table 1 cell summaries and header group sizes give harm-reduction means of 23.575 for older versus 22.974 for younger stories, 23.899 versus 22.652 within ecstasy stories, and 23.251 versus 23.299 within heroin stories. These support the authors' narrative direction and indicate that the two printed older-younger mean pairs are reversed. With a pooled within-cell SD of 4.927, approximate equal-marginal contrasts give F=4.63 for age, F=5.43 for age-by-drug and F=10.07 for age within ecstasy. The printed F=4.8 is therefore more consistent with the interaction than with the within-ecstasy age comparison in this reconstruction, but its exact identity cannot be established: the cell values are rounded, Table 1 header counts sum to 1248, and the reported residual degrees of freedom imply 1238 observations under the stated full eight-cell model. These F values are diagnostic editorial approximations, not an exact reanalysis. The older-younger contrast also changes the depicted person's drug-use history.
